sweep.help: map the address space by asking the machine

options.help: show this help message and exit
multiple of the measured reply time allowed before a probe is called a miss; a reply that outruns it is not lost, it arrives while the next probe is listening
an address known to answer; used both to calibrate reply timing and to tell a silent machine from a silent address
request sizes the reply timing is fitted over
repeat reads in the selftest that gates the sweep

write-probe.help: find what an address accepts by writing to it and reading it back

options.help: show this help message and exit
'40 01 30:24' probes 24 consecutive bytes from 40 01 30
probe every region an address map found, instead of naming them. The map is what the unit answered when it was asked, so this covers what exists rather than what a manual lists

for --map: keep only regions whose address starts with one of these, in the order given. A run long enough to be interrupted should meet the blocks that differ from each other before the ones that repeat
skip regions already in --out and add to it. A region is written as soon as it is finished, so an interrupted run resumes from the last whole region rather than from the start

an address known to answer, asked between regions. A unit that stops talking reads as a map of unreadable bytes, which is skipped rather than written to, so without this the probe finishes cleanly having measured nothing

read every address a saved run touched, compare it with what that run recorded it holding beforehand, and write the outcome back into the file. Writes nothing to the unit. A run restores as it goes and checks each region as it finishes, but only this sees the whole space at once and after the fact, which is what catches a byte left behind by a run that did not end on its own terms
pause between a write and the read back that checks it
write the result as JSON

window-probe.help: tell an address that holds a value from one that shows another address's, which writing to it and reading it back cannot

options.help: show this help message and exit

two addresses believed to hold their own values. Everything is measured relative to these, and they are asked as candidates too so a run that calls everything a window says so rather than reporting one
addresses to ask. Each is read after addressing each store in turn, and then written through to see which store the write reaches
pause after a write before the read that follows it
write the result as JSON

hold-probe.help: find whether neighbouring addresses hold their own values, by giving them different ones before reading any of them back

'20 00 00:64' asks 64 consecutive addresses from 20 00 00
ask every region an address map found, instead of naming them
for --map: keep only regions whose address starts with one of these, in order
pause after each write. Nothing is read until every write is done, so this is not a settle before a read back
write the result as JSON

address map read after each reset
where the addresses that take any value are read from. A partial probe leaves the marks partial, and a reset is then credited only across what was broken

mark only addresses starting here. Everything outside is left at whatever it held, so the run says nothing about it -- which is the bound to state when a subject is aimed at part of the space rather than at all of it
an address known to answer, asked while the marks go in. A unit that stops answering reads as one refusing every remaining mark, and the subject then scores for restoring a space the run never broke
what to break the state with. 'channel-mode' sends controllers 120, 121 and 123, which act rather than set and so cannot be measured by an alias scan's out-and-back

alias-scan.help: find where a message is stored, by diffing the address space around it

options.help: show this help message and exit
address map the watched regions are taken from

only watch regions whose address starts here. Every negative finding a run produces is bounded by what it watched, so a prefix turns 'this message is stored nowhere' into 'nowhere in the part of the space that was looked at'. The default watches all of it
zero based MIDI channel
what to send; two kinds landing on one address is what makes them aliases
for --kind address: bytes to write

for --kind address: take the bytes to write from what these alias scans attributed. Which addresses are worth asking a third way into is a finding about the unit, so it is read from that unit's own records rather than assumed
for --kind address: the two values written; both must be inside what the address accepts, or a clamp answers them identically and reads as storing nothing
drum note addressed one note at a time, for --kind drum-nrpn and for the key-based controls of --kind universal
controller numbers; default is 0 to 119
a controller known to be stored, always scanned, so a run that finds nothing can be told from a run that could not have found anything

repeat.help: find whether two takes of the same note can be compared, which every difference measurement rests on

options.help: show this help message and exit
zero based MIDI channel
seconds the note is held
length of each take
silence before the note; the noise floor is measured in it, so a residual has something it could not have gone below
seconds between takes
CC91 send during the takes
CC93 send during the takes
also hold one long note and read its frequency, which carries the unit's tuning and the two sample clocks' ratio together

options.help: show this help message and exit

three hex bytes to write instead, e.g. '40 01 30'
the two settings compared; both must be inside what the parameter accepts, or a clamp answers them identically and reads as inaudible
zero based MIDI channel

notes to ask the parameter under: struck, released, sustained, soft, loud, unpitched, wash, deep, struck_kit, struck_kit_map2, struck_moved, struck_retuned, struck_vibrato, low, high, plus 'broad' for the five that answer most parameters, 'switch' for the four a byte with two values needs, and 'all'. Recorded with the result, since the verdict only holds in the state it was taken in

directory to keep every take in, as float WAV with a manifest. Device time is the scarce thing here and a verdict thrown away with its audio has to be re-recorded to be asked anything else; kept takes can be measured again with the machine unplugged

interface inputs the return is captured on, counting from 1
length of the sweep
lowest frequency swept
highest frequency swept
silence recorded after the sweep, for the response to decay into. Too short and a reverb's tail wraps onto the start of its own impulse response

peak amplitude sent, 0 to 1. Half scale asks the input stage about its linear response; driving it to the rails measures its clipping instead, which is worth a run of its own at a stated level rather than by accident
sample rate for both directions

sweeps to run. One sweep cannot say whether its own numbers repeat, and a disturbance that comes and goes then reads as a property of the path: measured here, a single sweep put one channel's distortion 30 dB away from where ten further sweeps put it, with nothing in the printout to say which was which
the cable goes straight from output back to input, with the machine not in the path. Says so in the result, so a reference cannot be mistaken for a measurement of the machine
a WAV kept from a --loopback run, divided out of this one so what is left is the machine rather than the machine and the converters in series

state to put the machine in before the sweep, written over MIDI and read back to prove it took: '40 03 00=02 01' selects an insertion effect. Recorded with the result, since a response is a measurement of the state it was taken in and nothing in the returned audio says which state that was
seconds after each preparing write, before it is read back

directory to keep every take in, as float WAV with a manifest. Device time is the scarce thing here and a verdict thrown away with its audio has to be re-recorded to be asked anything else; kept takes can be measured again with the machine unplugged
write the result as JSON
